is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus s.s. (Page 2, Results).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (L1014F), Vgsc L995S (L1014S), Vgsc N1570Y (N1575Y), Ace-1 G280S (G119S), Rdl A296G (A296S), GSTe2 L119F, Cyp6p9a R, Cyp6p9b R, and Cyp6p9a/b 6.5kb-SV (Page 4, 7, 8).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype frequencies and counts are provided in Figures 4 and 5, and in the text (e.g., Page 4: 'The 296S-resistant allele (R) frequency was low (16.7%) with genotype frequency of 26.4% RS and 71.6% SS and 2% RR').

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in Ndjili-Brasserie, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo (Page 7, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study characterizing resistance profiles and molecular markers in 2021 field-collected mosquitoes.

sub_country_location.evidence: Collected in Ndjili-Brasserie, a suburb of Kinshasa (4° 19′ 39″ S, 15° 18′ 48″ E) (Page 7, Methods).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study explicitly states the collection occurred in July 2021 (Page 7, Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study is a new collection (2021) comparing results to a previous 2015 study (Riveron et al. 2018) in the same location.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data is present in the manuscript figures and text.

assessment.summary: This study characterizes the insecticide resistance profile and molecular markers of Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus s.s. collected in Kinshasa, DRC, in 2021, comparing findings to a 2015 baseline. It reports high pyrethroid resistance, near-fixation of kdr-w in A. gambiae, and increased frequency of GSTe2 in A. funestus.
